title: 第 41 課｜勞斯函數：一半哈密頓，一半拉格朗日｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
換變數的時候，有時我們只想把一部分廣義速度換成動量，其餘的保持不變。用的變換和上一課完全一樣，只是做到一半。為了讓式子短一點，假設只有兩個座標：一個叫 q，要換掉；一個叫 ξ，保持不變。寫出拉格朗日量的全微分，四個變數各一項。用動量的定義與拉格朗日方程處理前兩項，再把帶有 dq̇ 的那一項移到左邊，結果就是一個新量的全微分。這個量就是勞斯函數 R = p q̇ 減去 L，其中 q̇ 要用 p 表示出來。從它的全微分讀出係數會發現：對 q 與 p 這一對，它的行為完全像哈密頓方程——速度是 R 對動量的導數，動量的變化率是 R 對座標的導數的負值；對另一對 ξ 與它的速度，R 的導數等於拉格朗日量對應導數的負值，所以 ξ 的拉格朗日方程保持原樣。換句話說，勞斯函數對 q 像哈密頓量，對 ξ 像拉格朗日量。能量也可以用它寫出來：E = R 減去 v 乘上 R 對 v 的導數。座標更多時做法完全一樣。勞斯函數真正的用處是循環座標。循環座標不出現在拉格朗日量裡，因此也不出現在勞斯函數裡，於是勞斯函數只依賴那個座標的動量以及其餘的座標與速度；而循環座標對應的動量是常數，把這個常數值代進去之後，剩下的方程就只含剩下的座標——循環座標被完全消掉，自由度真的少了一個。解出剩下的座標之後，循環座標本身再由直接積分得到。中心力場是最經典的例子：角度是循環座標，它的動量就是守恆的角動量，剩下的只有有效位能裡的一維徑向運動。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 41 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 41 | The Routhian: Half Hamiltonian, Half Lagrangian | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
Sometimes, in changing variables, we want to replace only some of the generalised velocities by momenta and leave the rest alone. The transformation is exactly the one of the previous lesson, carried out only half way. To keep the formulas short, suppose there are just two coordinates: one called q, which will be transformed, and one called xi, which stays. Write the total differential of the Lagrangian, one term for each of the four variables. Use the definition of the momentum and Lagrange's equation on the first two terms, then move the term carrying the velocity differential across, and the result is the total differential of a new quantity. That quantity is the Routhian, R equal to p times q-dot minus L, with q-dot itself written in terms of the momentum. Reading the coefficients off its differential shows that for the pair q and p it behaves exactly as in Hamilton's equations: the velocity is the derivative of the Routhian with respect to the momentum, and the rate of change of the momentum is minus its derivative with respect to the coordinate. For the other pair, the derivatives of the Routhian with respect to xi and its velocity are minus the corresponding derivatives of the Lagrangian, so Lagrange's equation for xi keeps its form. In other words the Routhian is a Hamiltonian in q and a Lagrangian in xi. The energy can be written with it too: E equals R minus the velocity of xi times the derivative of R with respect to that velocity. With several coordinates everything works the same way. The Routhian earns its keep when some coordinates are cyclic. A cyclic coordinate does not appear in the Lagrangian and therefore not in the Routhian either, which then depends only on the momentum belonging to it together with the remaining coordinates and velocities. That momentum is a constant, and once its constant value is put in, the remaining equations contain only the remaining coordinates: the cyclic coordinate has been eliminated completely and the number of degrees of freedom really is reduced by one. Solve those equations for the remaining coordinate and the cyclic one then follows by direct integration. A central field is the classic case: the angle is cyclic, its momentum is the conserved angular momentum, and only one-dimensional radial motion in an effective potential is left.

Lesson 41 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
